title: Personal Credit Cards: card payment posted on the due date itself (autopay bank error test)
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: no payment posted on the due date

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When the ground for reversing a late payment fee on a card that carried an automatic payment instruction is decided, the bank error ground requires that no card payment posted to the card on the payment due date itself.

## Rule

1. The due date examined is the payment due date of the card's most recent statement.
2. The card payments whose posted date is that due date are counted.
3. The requirement holds only when that count is zero.

## Input, judgement, output

- **Input:** the card's payment entries and their posted dates; the payment due date of the card's most recent statement.
- **Judgement:** count the payments posted on exactly that due date.
- **Output:** zero payments on that date means the requirement holds; one or more means it fails.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, payment due date 28 June)

| Card payment posted | Counted for this requirement | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| none at all | no | holds |
| 27 June | no, it is not the due date | holds |
| 28 June | yes | fails |
| 29 June | no, it is not the due date | holds |

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Does a small payment on the due date matter if it did not cover the minimum?**
A: Yes. The requirement looks only at whether any card payment posted on the due date itself; one such payment, of any amount, makes the count one and the requirement fails.

**Q: Does a payment made a few days before the due date affect this requirement?**
A: No. Only a payment posted on the due date itself is counted here.
